audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer is built around 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)', which is not an Aurora ability. It appears 23 times, including focus.text, loading, breakdown.cooldowns and every report section. This is the second fabricated tracked-ability in my slice after Ambessa's 'Repeating Dashes'.
audit.why: Aurora's real abilities are Spirit Abjuration (P), Twofold Hex (Q), Across the Veil (W), The Weirding (E) and Between Worlds (R). 'Twofold Hunt' is a mashup of Twofold Hex's name with the blink concept that belongs to Across the Veil. The surrounding text is decisive about which was meant: every occurrence describes it as 'Her escape' and the '(Blink)' suffix, which is Across the Veil.
audit.corrected: Renamed all occurrences to 'Across the Veil (W)'. I kept the '(W)' suffix deliberately — 'Across the Veil' alone is five characters shorter than the fabricated name and would fail the applier's length band on the short strings such as focus.text and dosFull[0].t. With the slot suffix every occurrence lands inside the band.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)' and 'Across the Veil' as two separate abilities, describing both as her escape.
audit.why: They are the same ability. Renaming the fabricated entry alone would have produced a string that lists Across the Veil twice, so this one needed rewriting rather than renaming.
audit.corrected: Replaced the duplicate with The Weirding and its real 15s rank-1 cooldown, so the block now names her two genuinely distinct disengages with their real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers for Aurora appear anywhere, and the content layer treats her disengage as a single tool ('her E blink').
audit.why: She has two independent escapes on very different timers: The Weirding at 15/14/13/12/11s, whose damage-and-slow poke also hops her backwards as a side effect, and Across the Veil at 22/21/20/19/18s, which is a leap into invisibility. Against a champion with no dash and a 700-range Wither, the only thing that matters is whether BOTH are spent. Telling a Nasus to 'bait her E blink' as if there were one disengage is why players walk up into the second one.
audit.corrected: Rewrote content.mid, spikes[1], wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1] around counting both cooldowns, with the 15s and 22s rank-1 figures.

audit.whatIsWrong: Between Worlds is described only as 'ult realm' and 'level-6 ult realm', with no mechanical content.
audit.why: Riot's text: it 'creates an area that slows enemies within it and allows Aurora to teleport from one side of the area to the other'. That is an asymmetric zone — it slows Nasus while she crosses it freely. For the slowest champion in the matchup with no mobility, walking into that area is the single worst decision available at level 6, and nothing in the guide says so.
audit.corrected: Added the never-walk-through-it rule to content.mid and whys[4], and to wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds source despite _missing-interactions.json flagging needs-antiheal for this pairing.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration heals her from spirits exorcised by her own spells and attacks, which means she sustains passively off the same poke she is using to win the lane. This is a 46.31% matchup — Nasus's worst in this slice — and the late-game plan is an extended grinding duel, exactly the fight shape where her passive sustain compounds.
audit.corrected: Added to content.late, naming Spirit Abjuration.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] titled 'Build MR' was described as 'Aurora wastes Twofold Hunt (Blink) — commit the full pattern immediately'; dontsFull[1] titled 'Chase her blink' carried the same 'Burning your answer for tiny value...' string found on all four previous matchups.
audit.why: Five of five matchups audited so far carry the dontsFull[1].d paste defect. It is systematic across the Nasus file rather than a per-matchup slip, and is worth fixing at the generator level rather than one entry at a time.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both to match their titles.

audit.why: 46.31% over 434 games is the weakest matchup in this slice, and the chart [Skill, Aurora x5, Nasus] correctly gives her almost the whole lane. No chart contradiction was flagged and none is present. The 7/10 difficulty is if anything generous to Nasus, but I have no basis to propose a specific different number.

edits.before: Aurora hard-shoves nothing into you at level 1, so the first two levels are a farm race — soak Q stacks and let Soul Eater lifesteal eat her Q poke. The trap is her E blink: the instant you walk up to Wither her, she blinks back and chips you with Q on the way out. Don't chase a Q onto her — you'll only eat W exile and more poke. Last-hit at max range and accept that you concede the early window; you have no answer to a kiting AP who never stands in melee.
edits.after: Aurora shoves nothing into you at level 1, so the first two levels are a farm race — soak Q stacks and let Soul Eater lifesteal eat her Twofold Hex poke. The trap is The Weirding: the instant you walk up to Wither her, the blast slows you and hops her backwards out of range. Don't chase — you'll only eat Across the Veil and more poke. Last-hit at max range and accept that you concede the early window; you have no answer to a kiting AP who never stands in melee.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay hers. She pokes with Q, holds E to dodge anything you throw, and at 6 her ult realm plus W exile lets her zone you off the wave and burst your fat-but-squishy-early HP bar. Wither is your only mid-game tool — if she ever blinks toward you or whiffs the E, lock her down and Q immediately, because a slowed Aurora can't kite. Otherwise just stack: Spirit Fire (E) clears the wave and chips her, but don't expect to kill her until you have items. Take her ganks seriously since you can't disengage a root + realm.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay hers. She pokes with Twofold Hex, holds The Weirding to dodge anything you throw, and at 6 Between Worlds plus Across the Veil lets her zone you off the wave and burst your fat-but-squishy-early HP bar. She has two disengages, so count both — The Weirding is 15s and Across the Veil 22s at rank 1, and only once both are spent can you Wither and Q. Never walk through Between Worlds: it slows you inside it while she teleports across freely. Otherwise just stack with Spirit Fire.

edits.before: This is where you reclaim it. By 2+ items your Q stacks plus a Sheen/Iceborn proc one-shot her squishy frame, and Wither's full slow finally cancels the blink-and-kite that owned you all lane — one good W and she can't outrun your empowered Q or Fury of the Sands. Force the all-in the moment you have your first big item plus a few hundred stacks. Don't let her play for picks with her team — sidelane where her E blink can only escape, not reset, and grind her down with lifesteal.
edits.after: This is where you reclaim it. By 2+ items your Q stacks plus a Sheen/Iceborn proc one-shot her squishy frame, and Wither's full slow finally cancels the kiting that owned you all lane — one good Wither and she can't outrun your empowered Q or Fury of the Sands. Bring Grievous Wounds, because Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell she lands. Sidelane her, where Across the Veil can only escape and never reset, and grind her down with lifesteal.

notes: SECOND fabricated tracked-ability in this slice: 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)' across 23 strings on Aurora, after 'Repeating Dashes' across 23 strings on Ambessa. Both are recently-released champions and both fabrications sit in exactly the same set of fields (focus.text, loading, breakdown.*, dosFull[0].t, report[1]/[3]/[5]/[9]/[10]/[12]/[13]), which points at one generator pass that invented a plausible-sounding name whenever it lacked real ability data. Strongly recommend grepping every champion file for tracked-ability names that do not appear in the matching champ-data/_kits entry — my slice is 2 for 8 and I would expect the rest of the roster to be similar. The suspectNames detector cannot catch these because an invented name is not a near-miss of a real one; a set-membership check against the kit file would catch all of them. Naming choice worth a sanity check: I mapped 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)' to 'Across the Veil (W)' because every occurrence describes it as 'Her escape' and carries the '(Blink)' suffix. I kept the slot suffix on purpose so the replacement stays within the length band on the short fields — without it, focus.text and dosFull[0].t both fall below 0.9 and would be rejected. NOT ASSERTED: whether Aurora's spirit-realm state from Across the Veil can be revealed by a Control Ward or sweeper the way ordinary stealth can — the kit flags Across the Veil as a dash rather than stealth, and Riot's text says 'becoming invisible', which are different things in this game. I left the topic alone; it is worth a wiki pass because a Nasus who can reveal her has a very different lane. No WKM_LINES problems seen for this pairing.
